10 19-06-2023 I. A. No. 02 of 2023 This is an application for suspension of sentence and for releasing the applicant/appellant on bail during pendency of the appeal filed by him.
2. The appellant has renewed his request for grant of bail despite rejection of his earlier bail application on merit by the co-ordinate bench of this Court vide order dated 03.03.2017.

He is convicted of offences punishable under Sections 323, 341, 506 and 376(D) of the Indian Penal Code as well as under Section 4, 6 and 10 of the Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.

sentences.text: He is sentenced suitably on each count, Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.1168 of 2016(10) dt.19-06-2023 highest among which is imprisonment for life apart from imposition of some fine.
3. The learned counsel for the appellant argued that medical evidence is not supporting the version of the victim female child.

One of the witness has not Kamlesh Sahni vs The State Of Bihar on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42103736/

sentences.text: 4. None appeared for the State to oppose this bail application.
5. We have considered the submissions so advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant.
We are afraid that we cannot reopen merits of the case once co-ordinate bench of this Court has rejected bail application of the appellant on merits.

However, it needs to be noted that the victim female child who has been examined as P.W.8 by the prosecution has fully supported the case of commission of gang rape on her by stating that the appellant and the co-convict had committed penetrative sexual assault on her.
She has duly identified the appellant as the rapist.

6. The victim female child was subjected to medical examination which was conducted by P.W.-9 Dr.
Priti Gupta.

The medical report proved by this witness fully corroborates the Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.1168 of 2016(10) dt.19-06-2023 version of the victim female child.
Perusal of the medical report shows the brutal manner in which the victim female child was ravished by the appellant.
7. In this view of the matter, despite lapse of seven years' period of incarceration, as alleged by the learned counsel for the appellant, no case for grant of bail is made out.
8. The application is rejected.
However, hearing of the appeal be expedited.
9. Accordingly, I.A. No. 02 of 2023 stands disposed of.

(A. M. Badar, J)
 ( Harish Kumar, J)
